newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai April inflation rises less than expected.
newsitem.headline: Thai April inflation rises less than expected.

text.p: Thailand's consumer price index rose 4.3 percent year-on-year in April, the Thai Commerce Ministry said on Thursday.
Analysts said the figure was better than expected, as they had forecast inflation would rise about 4.5 to 4.6 percent on an annualised basis.
"That's a good number," said one analyst who had predicted 4.6 percent.
Inflation, which rose 0.2 percent on a monthly basis in April, was 4.5 percent year-on-year in March.
The Commerce Ministry said wholesale prices rose 0.9 percent year-on-year in April compared with a 1.1 percent increase the previous month.
Among consumer prices, rice and meat products were the biggest price gainers in the month, the ministry said.
There was no immediate market reaction to the announcement since markets were closed on Thursday for a Labour Day holiday.
The current trend shows Thai inflation for the year should come in below the 1996 figure of 5.9 percent.
